White supremacist (physical) propaganda.definition: Physical white supremacist propaganda includes distributions of physical media like fliers, posters, stickers, leaflets, banners and graffiti. The goal is to maximize media and online attention, while limiting the risk of individual exposure, negative media coverage, arrests and public backlash that often accompany public white supremacist events.

Q clock.definition: The Q clock is a tool used by QAnon followers to "prove" that Q has predicted future events. The Q clock consists of a standard clock surrounded by a line spiraling outwards, which features a series of dated points. Each point forms a "second" on the clock, and a shaded date indicates that Q posted a drop(s) on that date. To "read" the clock, QAnon followers draw a line from today's date on the spiral to the center of the clock, checking for any Q drops on shaded dates that the line intersects and decoding their meaning. The clock can also be "mirrored" by continuing to draw a line through to the other side of the clock, intersecting additional shaded dates and drops that can be decoded. The Q clock can only be used to confirm that Q predicted a future event in a prior drop; it cannot be used by QAnon followers to predict future events.

Red ink thumbprints.definition: Some sovereign citizens believe they must place a thumbprint or fingerprint next to their signature on a document for it to be valid. Most, though not all, who hold such beliefs further claim that the signature and fingerprint must be in red ink.The origins of the sovereign citizen thumbprint idea date back to the late 1980s, though it only became popular in the 1990s. In some societies at some points in history, such prints were used as signatures or were required to accompany signatures.

Black Bloc Tactics.definition: Black bloc tactics are often employed by militant antifa adherents at protests. Participants dressed in all black will operate as a unified force. Tactics include arming themselves with riot shields and positioning themselves at the front while others behind them move "like water."

Media Jihad.definition: "Media jihad" refers to an ISIS innovation in the Islamist terrorist sphere heavily emphasizing online media and appealing propaganda as a means of recruiting foreign fighters and spreading its message. To this end, ISIS recruiters often emphasize that "media jihad," creating and spreading ISIS propaganda online, is just as effective a method of supporting the caliphate as traveling to conflict zones.

Nutella and Kittens.definition: Nutella and kittens was among ISIS's more inventive and disturbing media tactics. In 2015, the group paired calls to join the Islamic State with innocuous images that were popular on the internet, including pictures of kittens or jars of Nutella. One New Jersey-based ISIS recruiter even went by the online nickname "Umm Nutella," meaning "Mother of Nutella." Though it is unclear whether this tactic was effective at increasing recruitment, it generated a great deal of attention for ISIS online.

Paper Terrorism.definition: "Paper terrorism" is a term given to a range of tactics developed by the sovereign citizen movement to use against their perceived enemies. These tactics typically involve the filing of bogus legal documents or the misuse of legal documents in a way designed to harass, retaliate against or harm police, government officials and others. Common paper terrorism tactics include bogus liens, false IRS 1099 forms, false involuntary bankruptcies and false criminal complaints, among others.
